title: Y-coordinate after a y-stretch then a vertical translation
source: Theory P1-2.8 Quick check 1 (point (0, 1) maps to (0, 5) after stretch factor 3 then translation +2); new positive factors and translations
stem: The point \((0, 1)\) lies on the graph of \(y=f(x)\). A stretch of scale factor {a|int} parallel to the \(y\)-axis is applied, then a translation of {b|int} units in the positive \(y\)-direction. What is the \(y\)-coordinate of the image of this point?

steps.name: A
steps.text_tex: The stretch sends \((0, 1)\) to \((0, {a|int})\). The translation then adds {b|int}, giving \(y\)-coordinate \({a|int}+{b|int}={A|int}\).
steps.note: A is a+b. Original a=3, b=2 gives 5.

title: Coefficient after an x-stretch of y=x squared then a y-stretch
source: Theory P1-2.8 Quick check 2 (stretch x-factor 1/2 then y-factor 3 on y=x^2 gives y=12x^2); new y-stretch factors
stem: The graph of \(y=x^2\) is stretched by scale factor \(\dfrac{1}{2}\) parallel to the \(x\)-axis and then by scale factor {a|int} parallel to the \(y\)-axis. The resulting graph has equation \(y=cx^2\). What is the value of \(c\)?

steps.name: A
steps.text_tex: Replacing \(x\) by \(2x\) gives \(y=(2x)^2=4x^2\). Multiplying by {a|int} then gives \(y={A|int}x^2\), so \(c={A|int}\).
steps.note: A is 4a. Original a=3 gives c=12.

title: Y-stretch factor from a combined equation y=a f(x-1)
source: Theory P1-2.8 Quick check 3 (in y=2f(x-1) the y-stretch factor is 2); new positive factors
stem: The graph of \(y=f(x)\) is translated by 1 unit in the positive \(x\)-direction and then stretched by scale factor {a|int} parallel to the \(y\)-axis, giving \(y={a|int}f(x-1)\). What is the scale factor of the stretch parallel to the \(y\)-axis?

steps.name: A
steps.text_tex: The factor multiplying the function is {A|int}, which is the scale factor of the stretch parallel to the \(y\)-axis.
steps.note: A equals a. Original a=2 gives 2.

title: Equation after a stretch, a reflection and a second stretch

source.note: Stem taken from the QP PDF (UCLES 2023), Question 2, including the scale factor 1/2 verified on the official page. Official answer and mark allocation from the MS PDF. The item is paper/self-mark.

stem:
This question is 9709/12/F/M/23 Question 2, taken from the official QP.

A function \(f\) is defined by \(f(x)=x^2-2x+5\) for \(x\in\mathbb{R}\). A sequence of transformations is applied in the following order to the graph of \(y=f(x)\) to give the graph of \(y=g(x)\).

Stretch parallel to the \(x\)-axis with scale factor \(\dfrac{1}{2}\)

Reflection in the \(y\)-axis

Stretch parallel to the \(y\)-axis with scale factor 3

Find \(g(x)\), giving your answer in the form \(ax^2+bx+c\), where \(a\), \(b\) and \(c\) are constants.  [4]

steps.name: S
steps.text_tex: The stretch of scale factor \(\dfrac{1}{2}\) parallel to the \(x\)-axis replaces \(x\) by \(2x\): \((2x)^2-2(2x)+5=4x^2-4x+5\).
steps.note: Official MS Q2: M1 for replacing x by 2x, or the completed-square form leading to (2x-1)^2+4.

steps.name: R
steps.text_tex: The reflection in the \(y\)-axis then replaces \(x\) by \(-x\): \(4(-x)^2-4(-x)+5=4x^2+4x+5\).
steps.note: Official MS Q2: M1 for replacing x by -x, follow through on their stretch.

steps.name: Y
steps.text_tex: The stretch of scale factor 3 parallel to the \(y\)-axis multiplies the whole function by 3: \(g(x)=3(4x^2+4x+5)\).
steps.note: Official MS Q2: M1 for multiplying the whole function by 3, follow through on their stretch plus reflection.

steps.name: A
steps.note: Official MS Q2: A1 for 12x^2+12x+15. Independent: 3(4x^2+4x+5)=12x^2+12x+15.
